scenes.text: There's a tiny animal that survived the vacuum of open space.
Tardigrades, or water bears, are usually less than a millimeter long.
In two thousand seven, scientists sent dried-out tardigrades into orbit on an uncrewed satellite.
They were exposed to space for ten days.
Back on Earth, many came back to life with water, and some even laid eggs that hatched.
Their secret is drying into a tough little ball called a tun, where their metabolism almost stops.
What tiny animal should we cover next?

title: This tiny animal survived the vacuum of space 🚀
caption: In 2007, dried-out tardigrades rode the FOTON-M3 satellite and were exposed to open space for 10 days. Many revived after rehydration and some still reproduced (Jönsson et al., Current Biology 2008). 🐻
